title.value: Augmenting Human Selves Through Artificial Agents – Lessons From the Brain
title.justification: The paper focuses on enhancing human capacities through artificial agents, which are informed by the functioning of the human brain, specifically through the use of the free energy principle and temporo-spatial dynamics.
title.quote: Augmenting Human Selves Through Artificial Agents – Lessons From the Brain

extractions.description: This paper explores how artificial agents can augment human capabilities, focusing on personal capacities such as wellbeing and morality. The authors propose integrating the free energy principle and temporo-spatial dynamics from brain processes into artificial agents to allow for adaptive alignment with varying environments. The aim is to improve human capacities, including mental health support, disaster prediction, and moral decision-making.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on augmenting human intelligence and capacities using artificial agents modeled on brain functions. While there is a mention of using such agents for predicting environmental disasters, this is not the main theme of the paper.
climate_change_is_central.quote: The targeted applications are broad: from adaptive intelligence augmenting agents (IA’s) that assist psychiatric self-regulation to environmental disaster prediction and personal assistants.

primary_category.justification: The main focus of the paper is on enhancing human capabilities through artificial agents, which is not directly aligned with any primary climate change category. The mention of predicting natural disasters does not centralize Climate Change as the main focus.
primary_category.quote: This reflects the central role of the mind and moral decision-making in most of what we do as humans.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper mentions applications in predicting environmental disasters, which is a concern of climate science. Although not central to the paper, it is relevant as a secondary focus.
secondary_categories.quote: especially in the age of climate change, we require tools to properly predict such environmental crises well.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category aligning directly with the core focus of the paper, which is enhancing human capabilities through artificial agents.
primary_sub_category.quote: We focus on how a machine can augment humans rather than do what they do, and we extend this beyond AGI-style tasks to augmenting peculiarly personal human capacities, such as wellbeing and morality.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Although not the main emphasis, the paper refers to the need for predicting natural disasters in the context of climate change, which fits this sub-category within Climate Science.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Especially in the age of climate change, we require tools to properly predict such environmental crises well ahead of time in a more fine-grained way.

applications.justification: The paper mentions using the proposed artificial agents with adaptive capacities to enhance the prediction of natural disasters, an application relevant to climate change adaptation and risk management.
applications.quote: wildfire prediction could thus incorporate these variables over a long temporal range that, as such, is not accessible to humans.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories do not fit the main focus of the paper, which is on human capacity augmentation through artificial agents.
new_primary_category.quote: We base this proposal on associating such capacities with the “self,” which we define as the “environment-agent nexus”; namely, a fine-tuned interaction of brain with environment in all its relevant variables.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There's no need for a new sub-category as the paper primarily targets human augmentation through AI, which doesn't directly align with the existing climate change sub-categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: the brain’s TSD is organized in a hierarchical manner, according to time and space scales, which are adaptively determined and finely nested.
